newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farmers fear heavy income losses.
newsitem.headline: German farmers fear heavy income losses.

text.p: German farmers predict sharp income losses as a result of the mad cow disease crisis and lower milk prices in 1996/97 (July/June), a statement from farm union DBV said on Tuesday.
"Unless the ailing beef market can be stabilised within the next few weeks and months, farmers' income losses may exceed those forecast by the government," it said.

The statement came in response to the agriculture ministry's annual report, which said incomes might fall by between two and six percent after an average 6.6 percent rise in 1995/96 to 53,973 marks per full-time farm.
DBV called for government support to overcome the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) crisis.
DBV rejected government plans to reduce spending on agriculture and to abolish certain tax breaks.
